issues_encountered: SRAM_SKY130 read FSM asserted s_rvalid/s_rdata one cycle before the sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 macro's negedge-launched dout1 was actually stable for posedge sampling -- reads returned stale data and silently dropped the true final burst beat (6/10 sram_controller unit tests FAIL under SRAM_TARGET=sky130); root cause: dout1 becomes posedge-sampleable TWO cycles after address issue (negedge production mid-cycle N+1, settled by posedge N+2), not one, but the single-stage rd_dv_q pipeline exposed it after only one cycle.

MEM_WORDS!=1024 guard used `initial $error(...)`, a simulation-time construct that never fires under `verilator --lint-only` elaboration (no simulation is run), so a future wrong MEM_WORDS override would silently truncate onto the macro's 10-bit addr0/addr1 with no warning at all under lint.
fixes_applied: Added a second pipeline stage (rd_pend_q/rd_pend_last_q marking 'macro negedge write for this address is happening this cycle') feeding a new 2-entry output skid buffer (buf_v_q/buf_last_q/buf_data_q, slot0=AXI-facing head, slot1=one-beat overflow reserve for backpressure). s_rvalid/s_rdata/s_rlast now source from the buffer, not directly from rd_dv_q/mem_dout1. Issue gating changed from single-slot occupancy to buf_has_room (slot1 guaranteed free after this cycle's drain/fill), preserving full 1-beat/cycle sustained throughput (slot1 unused in the no-backpressure steady state; only engaged when RREADY toggles off mid-burst) while guaranteeing no drop/duplicate/early-RLAST under arbitrary backpressure patterns. R_BUSY->R_IDLE now waits for the whole pipeline (r_active, rd_pend_q, both buffer slots) to fully drain before accepting a new AR.

Hardened the MEM_WORDS!=1024 guard: replaced `initial $error(...)` with a bare `$fatal(1, ...)` directly inside the generate `if` scope (no `initial` wrapper) -- this is an IEEE 1800-2017 section 20.11 'elaboration system task', evaluated at elaboration time rather than simulation time. Confirmed via standalone `verilator --lint-only -GMEM_WORDS=2048`: the message now fires and prints (USERFATAL) purely from elaboration, and without the project's `-Wno-fatal` lint flag it also gives EXIT_CODE=1. Caveat: this project's `sim/Makefile` lint targets pass `-Wno-fatal` globally, so a future MEM_WORDS misconfiguration would print visibly but not hard-fail the `make lint` exit code -- worth a separate follow-up if hard CI gating on this specific check is wanted (out of scope for this surgical fix).
notes: Serviced fix_request fr_null_20260724_051800_00 (GH #104 Sky130 SoC Stage-2). Lint-only validated in this session (make -C sim lint_soc_sky130: 0 errors, 0 new warnings vs baseline). Cocotb re-run (baseline + SRAM_SKY130 suites, including new test_read_backpressure_no_drop_no_dup) intentionally deferred to verification-orchestrator per project policy -- not run here. Not committed per instruction. Key generalizable pattern: when wrapping a negedge-launched/registered-output hard macro behind a single-cycle-ahead 'address-ahead' skid-buffer FSM, always derive the posedge-to-posedge sampling latency from the macro's own capture-then-launch timing (posedge capture + negedge launch = 2 posedge-sampled cycles from a naive 'presented this cycel' baseline), not from a verbal 1-cycle-latency assumption in the macro's docstring/header comment -- and preserve sustained beat/cycle throughput under a 2-cycle unstoppable production pipeline via a small (depth = pipeline_depth) output skid FIFO gated on 1-cycle-ahead occupancy prediction, not a single valid/last register pair.

issues_encountered: GH #93 (commit 66a9af1) introduced a CPU-domain CDC clock-gate enable synchroniser (cdc_2ff_sync) whose SAFE (reset-to-0) value meant 'clock disabled' -- reset was rooted at cpu_core_rst_n, so cpu_gated_clk never toggled for the entire cpu_domain_rst_n-low window, and u_cpu's synchronous reset () never executed, so RESET_PC never loaded. Root cause: the OTHER half of the domain reset AND (pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync, fed by pmu_cpu_rst_n which defaults to 1 out of pmu.sv reset) filled to 1 almost immediately regardless of cpu_core_rst_n, so the composite cpu_domain_rst_n tracked cpu_core_rst_n almost exactly and released on the very edge the clock-enable sync was still 2 cycles from opening the gate. Second manifestation: the CDC bridge (async_axi_fifo) s-side face shares the same s_clk_i=cpu_gated_clk, so its internal cdc_reset_sync had the identical starvation, violating the fifo's documented >= SYNC_STAGES+1-clk-periods reset-hold contract.
fixes_applied: Inverted the clock-enable CDC synchroniser: synchronise ~pmu_cpu_clk_en into pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync instead of pmu_cpu_clk_en directly, so cdc_2ff_sync's reset-to-0 default now means 'not disabled' (clock running) -- matching the actually-required safe state -- instead of 'disabled'. Gate enable becomes ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync. General pattern: when a clock-gate enable is synchronised with a primitive whose reset value is fixed (e.g. cdc_2ff_sync always resets to 0), pick the polarity so that reset value IS the safe state for the consumer -- for an enable gating a clock that must keep ticking through the consumer's own reset, that means synchronising the inverted/disable sense, not the raw enable.

issues_encountered: GH #93 fix_request fr_280f3ac18c66: cdc_gray_fifo.sv wr_ready_o = !full_q was not gated by wr_rst_n_i. full_q resets to 1'b0 ('not full'), so wr_ready_o read 1 for the ENTIRE window the write domain was held in reset -- while wr_bin_q/wr_gray_q were also held at their reset values by the same reset. A write master could complete a handshake (wr_valid_i && wr_ready_o) during this window whose beat was then silently dropped (never committed, since the clocked push logic's else branch never executes while !wr_rst_n_i). Only reachable at a genuinely asynchronous dual-clock ratio (GH #93's CPU:fabric split) where one domain's PLL-lock reset releases while the other domain's reset is still asserted -- invisible at the previously-only-tested 1:1 ratio. Confirmed empirically at SoC level via verification's ns-resolution diagnostic (CPU's first AR handshake falsely completed, response never arrived, CPU hung forever).

Fixing this correctly (wr_ready_o = wr_rst_n_i && !full_q) causes ONE pre-existing GH #91 unit test (test_reset_while_busy_s_side in tb/cocotb/soc/test_async_axi_fifo.py) to newly fail (21/22, was 22/22). issues_encountered: pmu.sv power-up sequencing (reset-release-before-clock-ungate, UPF-mandated retention-by-construction) crosses into the CPU cpu_core_clk domain through two SEPARATE CDC synchronisers (cdc_reset_sync for rst, cdc_2ff_sync for clk_en). Two independent synchronisers do not preserve a 1-core_clk-cycle source-side offset; a live firmware-driven PMU power-cycle could let the CPU clock resume at or before the domain reset release is observed, spuriously firing the CPU synchronous reset branch and silently overwriting retained architectural state (PC/MSTATUS/MTVEC) with RESET_PC/RESET_VAL -- same failure class as the GH #93 cold-boot bug (4398c2e) but on the power-cycle path instead, and NOT visible to any 1:1-ratio or cold-boot-only regression.
fixes_applied: Fixed in soc_top.sv, NOT pmu.sv (pmu.sv sequencing order is UPF-mandated per docs/POWER_DOMAIN_EVALUATION.md section 3 and pmu.sv header -- changing it would either violate the UPF intent or defeat the no-retention-hardware trick). Derived cpu_gated_clk_en = ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync (a same-domain, already-registered combinational AND, no new CDC crossing) and used it as u_cpu_cg enable. This makes the already-synchronised domain reset the master gating term for the domain clock, structurally forbidding a clock edge while that reset is asserted regardless of the relative skew between the two independent synchronisers -- unbounded skew tolerance, symmetric for power-up and power-down. General pattern: when two independently-synchronised control signals from the SAME source domain must preserve a relative order downstream (e.g. reset-then-clock, or any A-before-B invariant), do not rely on synchroniser latency matching -- instead derive the dependent signal (clock enable) as a function of the ALREADY cross-domain-synchronised independent signal (reset), so the invariant is enforced by construction in the destination domain, not by hoping the two crossings resolve in the same relative order they started in.

issues_encountered: GH #93 apb_cdc_bridge.sv: s_rst_sync_n was rooted in rst_both_n = s_rst_n_i & m_rst_n_i, so the SOURCE domain FSM was held in S_IDLE for as long as the DESTINATION domain's own reset (m_rst_n_i) stayed asserted -- an APB access to the CPU-domain PLL2 window during a CPU-only reset permanently wedged the entire fabric APB tree (UART/SPI/timer/IRQ/PMU/both PLL blocks), since a held-in-reset FSM cannot even emit an error response. Found by CodeRabbit on PR #132, independently verified.

First fix attempt (fully decoupling BOTH cdc_reset_sync instances from each other's reset) was analysed and rejected before implementation: it reproduces a silent-drop hang on the first post-reset request whenever an odd number of transfers had completed before an s-only reset, because req_toggle_q (source) and req_seen_q (destination) lose their toggle-parity invariant.

First lint/sim pass of the corrected design (m_rst_n_i synchronised active-low into the source domain, default reset-to-0 = 'presumed in reset') passed apb_cdc_bridge_lint and 13/15 tests, but FAILED test_clock_ratio_slow_s_fast_m (18ns/4ns) on txn 0 -- a genuine regression, not a test-encodes-old-behavior case. Root cause: chaining a second cdc_2ff_sync (reset by the already-synchronised s_rst_sync_n) after the first stacks TWO synchronisers' settling latency in series on every post-reset transaction, and the existing test's reset-recovery margin (3 cycles) was tuned for only one synchroniser's settle time.
fixes_applied: Asymmetric reset decoupling: s_rst_sync_n (source domain) rooted on s_rst_n_i ONLY; m_rst_sync_n (destination domain) deliberately LEFT on rst_both_n = s_rst_n_i & m_rst_n_i -- the coupling is still genuinely required in that direction to keep req_seen_q's toggle bookkeeping consistent across an s-only reset.

New single-bit destination-reset-status synchroniser (cdc_2ff_sync) gates whether a request is ever forwarded (req_fwd_q latched at SETUP), bounds S_WAIT so it always resolves (ack_new | !req_fwd_q | destination-observed-in-reset), and continuously clamps req_toggle_q to 0 while the destination is observed in reset -- closing the fabricated-write hazard (an errored request's stale toggle value must never later be misread by the destination as a fresh request once it exits reset).

POLARITY FIX after first regression: synchronise the ACTIVE-HIGH 'destination in reset' sense (~m_rst_n_i), not m_rst_n_i directly, so the synchroniser's fixed reset-to-0 default means 'presumed alive' (matching steady-state truth immediately) instead of 'presumed in reset' (which silently stacked a second synchroniser's settle latency onto every post-reset transaction). This is the generalizable lesson: when adding a NEW synchroniser whose reset is itself driven by an already-synchronised reset signal (i.e. serially chained), always choose the polarity so the synchroniser's fixed hardware reset-default equals the expected STEADY-STATE value, not the fault-condition value -- otherwise the good path silently inherits the bad path's settle latency, and only shows up on the slowest clock ratio in the test matrix.

issues_encountered: bead rvb Path A first iteration (word_sel_q registered one-hot) still left s_wvalid as a same-cycle combinational source for a MEM_WORDS-wide AND array gating every mem[] storage bit -- post-route measurement showed it remained the #1 setup-violator class (16400 violators, worst -1050.16 ps) despite being a registered decode.

A single shared registered signal (even if narrowed from per-bit to per-word AND gates) still has fan-out proportional to MEM_WORDS if every word listens to the same commit register directly -- the fix had to break BOTH the decode width AND the physical distribution (per-group local registers), not just add one register stage.

Yosys opt_merge can silently collapse structurally-identical replicated registers (e.g. NGROUPS copies of a per-group register bank) back into one high-fanout register if every copy has the exact same D-input logic -- defeating a fan-out-distribution fix at synthesis time without any RTL-visible symptom.

Prevented Yosys opt_merge from collapsing the per-group stage-2 replicas by giving each group register a self-holding D-input (grp_wdata_q[k] <= sel ? new_data : grp_wdata_q[k]) instead of an unconditional load -- this makes every group instance structurally distinct even though they are functionally parallel copies. Verified directly: standalone yosys synth (opt -fast -full; opt_merge -share_all) showed 0 cells removed.

Delayed BVALID via a new drain FSM state until the pipeline has actually landed the burst's last beat in mem[], so B-respecting masters (wait for B before same-address AR) are safe by construction despite the new multi-cycle write-commit latency -- verified with a directed cocotb test asserting immediate-read-after-B correctness.
